description.narrative: (Angola): Health For All (HFA) supports access and quality of health systems delivery through training and supervision, malaria prevention, including facility and community-level case management, social behavior change, malaria epidemiological and entomological surveillance strengthening, and National Malaria Control Program (NMCP) capacity building, including the use of the District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2) data platform. HFA will continue to support insecticide-treated bed net distribution campaigns, along with building NMCP's capacity to conduct national campaigns to cover Angola's remaining 10 provinces; implementation of activities to increase antenatal care uptake and improve communication between healthcare workers and caregivers. HFA will continue implementing entomological monitoring, including both insecticide resistance and community-based vector bionomic surveillance. HFA will also continue to implement FP/RH activities in four provinces namely: Huambo Malange, Luanda, and Lunda Sul. An integrated approach between Malaria and FP/RH will be implemented in Malange and Lunda Sul provinces, ensuring the health facilities model is transitioned to the local government. Based on funding and MoH priorities, activities might be extended to other provinces. HFA will disseminate existing policies and guidelines on healthy timing and spacing of pregnancy and gender-based violence; increase use of the Health Network Quality Improvement System monitoring tool to local government; increase demand for long-acting FP methods; continue the FP/RH Digital Campaign for youth; and support the MoH to develop a costed national implementation plan for FP services, and recommitting to the FP 2030 Initiative. HFA will continue to support health systems strengthening through improving accuracy, timeliness, completeness, and use of data for decision making of malaria and family planning data reported through DHIS2 platform.

Objectives for Angola: The project aims for a 40 percent reduction in malaria through nationwide insecticide-treated net distribution campaigns and improvement of the quality of clinical malaria services; 90 percent of people living with HIV placed on treatment in Luanda with the establishment of a sustainable model for quality HIV/AIDS services; 30 percent to 53 percent increase in national use of contraceptives as a result of high-level technical assistance in family planning/sexual and reproductive health; Technicians’ capacity to develop and monitor health budgets at the provincial and municipal level to develop and monitor health budgets will be strengthened.
